title: States Weekly: October 28, 2026
gist: CSIS's weekly digest of Indian state policy highlights power-sector liberalization (Haryana grants Eleven Power a 25-year parallel distribution license, the state's first private distributor), EV and rooftop-solar incentives in Delhi, Meghalaya and Gujarat, and sharp aviation turbine fuel VAT cuts in Tamil Nadu and Goa. Goa also floated a draft three-year AI policy.

themes.theme: Indian power distribution opening to private players

insights.claim: Haryana approved a 25-year parallel electricity distribution license for Eleven Power covering Gurugram and Nuh, making it the first private power distributor to operate in the state.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Parallel licensing in a high-demand corridor like Gurugram signals gradual privatization of Indian discoms, a potential opening for private utility investors.
insights.quote: Eleven Power will become the first private distributor to operate in Haryana.

insights.claim: Telangana launched a one-time settlement scheme for industries to clear pending electricity dues, with utilities hoping to recover about $210.6 million (INR 2,000 crore).
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Points to persistent receivables stress at Indian state utilities, a key credit risk for the power value chain.
insights.quote: Utilities hope to recover about $210.6 million (INR 2,000 crore) through the initiative.

themes.theme: State-level EV and rooftop solar incentives

insights.claim: Delhi's draft E-Rickshaw Scheme 2026 seeks to regulate e-rickshaw operations and the city is considering capping the fleet at 250,000 vehicles with mandatory compliance certifications.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A fleet cap could constrain unit growth for low-speed EV makers in India's largest e-rickshaw market while favoring certified, compliant manufacturers.
insights.quote: Delhi is also considering a cap of 250,000 e-rickshaws in Delhi, with mandatory compliance certifications to follow.

insights.claim: Gujarat added a state subsidy for residential rooftop solar systems up to 2.18 kWp that caps household cost at 5 percent of benchmark for SC/ST households and 10 percent for others, topping up the central PM Surya Ghar subsidy.
insights.speaker: CSIS
entities: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
insights.so_what: Near-free rooftop solar in Gujarat should accelerate residential installations, supportive for Indian solar module and inverter suppliers.
insights.locator: Gujarat approves an extra state subsidy

insights.claim: Meghalaya's Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 offers purchase incentives, motor vehicle tax and registration fee exemptions, and scrappage benefits to drive EV adoption.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: EV incentive policies are spreading even to smaller northeastern states, broadening India's EV demand base.
insights.locator: Meghalaya notifies its Electric Vehicle Policy

insights.claim: Tamil Nadu cut VAT on aviation turbine fuel for scheduled domestic airlines from 29 percent to 16 percent at Chennai Airport and to 1 percent at other airports in the state.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Lower ATF taxes reduce fuel costs for Indian domestic airlines and may shift route economics toward Tamil Nadu's secondary airports.
insights.quote: VAT at Chennai Airport has been reduced from 29 percent to 16 percent, and at other airports to 1 percent for scheduled domestic airlines.

insights.claim: Goa set a 7 percent VAT rate on aviation turbine fuel effective October 24, joining Tamil Nadu in lowering ATF taxation.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Multiple states competing on ATF tax suggests a broader trend of lower airline fuel costs in India.

insights.claim: Goa published a draft Artificial Intelligence Policy running 2026 to 2029 focused on building AI skills, supporting startups and attracting investment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Sub-national AI policies indicate Indian states competing for AI startup and investment flows.
insights.locator: Goa publishes a draft Artificial Intelligence

insights.claim: Andhra Pradesh revamped its Development Permission Management System to automate scrutiny of Occupancy Certificate applications and release of mortgage-related documents, aiming to cut approval times and human intervention.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Faster occupancy approvals can shorten real estate project cycles and improve developer cash conversion in the state.

themes.theme: Urban growth and state fiscal measures

insights.claim: Telangana extended its 2020 Integrated Township Policy by five years to steer Hyderabad's growth toward large self-contained townships on the city's outskirts.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Continued policy support for peripheral townships favors land-bank-heavy developers around Hyderabad.

insights.claim: Himachal Pradesh raised dearness allowance for state government employees by 5 percent.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Adds to state wage bill pressure, relevant for Indian state fiscal health.
